(Montverde, Florida) | college = [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] (2022–2023) | highlights = * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (2023) * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team (2023) * Second-team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] (2023) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2022) * 2× [[High School Showcase|GEICO High School National champion]] (2021, 2022) }} '''Jalen Hood-Schifino''' (born June 19, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He previously played for [[Montverde Academy]]. Hood-Schifino was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and ranked as the highest incoming [[Big Ten]] recruit for the class of 2022. ==High school career== Hood-Schifino played for three different programs in high school. He began his prep career at [[Northside Christian Academy]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]]. As a sophomore, Hood-Schifino played at Combine Academy in [[Lincolnton, North Carolina]]. Before his junior season, Hood-Schifino transferred to national powerhouse [[Montverde Academy]] in Florida, coached by Kevin Boyle. At Montverde, Hood-Schifino won back-to-back [[High School Showcase|GEICO High School Basketball National titles]] (2021 and 2022). Hood-Schifino was named an all-star and invited to play in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], where he scored 14 points and hit three three-point shots. In the off-season prior to college he also played for coach Norton Hurd IV and Team Thad, an AAU program founded by NBA player [[Thaddeus Young]]. He spent time working out in [[California]] with professionals, including the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]’ [[Paul George]]. Hood-Schifino stated that his time at Montverde prepared him for college basketball, noting, "The everyday grind at Montverde, people don’t really know what’s, you know, put into it, like the practices. It's almost like a college practice; you're practicing three-plus hours every day, so it really prepared me for now. . . Now going through college, it’s almost like I’m at Montverde but at a college level." ===Recruiting=== While playing at the Combine Academy, Hood-Schifino committed to play for [[Jeff Capel]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]]. At the time, it was considered a major recruiting win for the Panthers to land Hood-Schifino, a Pittsburgh native. But following Hood-Schifino's sophomore year in high school, he chose to reopen his recruitment. The [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] became involved in Hood-Schifino’s recruitment in the summer of 2021, just months after head coach [[Mike Woodson]] began in Bloomington. Hood-Schifino committed to the Hoosiers in August of 2021. He was the highest-rated recruit to sign with the Hoosiers since [[Romeo Langford]] in 2018 and the 9th highest-ranked recruit for the program since 1998. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Jalen Hood-Schifino | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania|Pittsburgh, PA]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (Montverde, FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 215 | 40 = | commitdate = August 24, 2021 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 91 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2022 | rivals ref title = Indiana 2022 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2022 Indiana Hoosiers Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = Indiana | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 84 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 17 | 247 overall = 22 | espn overall = 24 | accessdate = October 19, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Prior to Hood-Schifino's freshman year with the Hoosiers, a mock NBA draft projected him as a first-round pick. A panel of Big Ten media named him the preseason freshman of the year in the league.{{cite news |last1=Bozich |first1=Alex |title=2022-23 Indiana basketball player profile: Jalen Hood-Schifino |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2022/10/17/2022-23-indiana-basketball-player-profile-jalen-hood-schifino/ |access-date=19 October 2022 |agency=Inside the Hall}} In his [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|lone season]] at Indiana, Hood-Schifino was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Year and third team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media. In 32 games (32 starts), he averaged 13.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists in 33.1 minutes per game. On January 8, 2023, Hood-Schifino scored 33 points in a 84-83 loss against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] at [[Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall|Assembly Hall]], the most points by a freshman at Indiana since [[Eric Gordon]] against [[Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball|Chattanooga]] in 2007. On February 25, 2023, Hood-Schifino scored an Indiana freshman-record 35 points in a 79-71 win against [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] at [[Mackey Arena]]. On March 31, 2023, Hood-Schifino declared for the [[NBA draft]], foregoing his final three years of college eligibility. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] | 32 || 32 || 33.1 || .417 || .333 || .776 || 4.1 || 3.7 || 0.3 || 0.8 || 13.5 |- class="sortbottom" {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Hood-Schifino is the son of Glenn Hood and Adrianne "Angel" Hood-Schifino. The family was originally in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania|Pittsburgh]], but moved to Charlotte while Hood-Schifino was in middle school. Growing up, he played basketball in his grandparents’ backyard and played against his older cousins, Sherron and DeAndre Schifino. DeAndre would end up being a member of the University of Pittsburgh’s football team. Sherron Schifino would end up playing college basketball. Sherron and DeAndre Schifino’s friends — who were also older than Hood-Schifino — played with them, too. "I was always the young kid," Hood-Schifino later explained.{{cite news |last1=Tachmann |first1=Tyler |title=Jalen Hood-Schifino brings competitiveness, versatility to Indiana |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2022/06/24/jalen-hood-schifino-brings-competitiveness-versatility-to-indiana/ |access-date=19 October 2022 |agency=Inside the Hall |date=June 24, 2022}} As part of a [[student athlete compensation]] package to raise awareness for Indiana charity partners, Hood-Schifino endorsed Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Indiana, offering in-person appearances (such as speaking, presentation of skills, autograph sessions, and the like) as well as social media posts promoting these appearances and the charity.{{cite news |title=11 IU basketball athletes join summer class for Hoosiers For Good NIL deal |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2022/08/03/11-iu-basketball-athletes-join-summer-class-for-hoosiers-for-good-nil-deal/ |access-date=19 October 2022 |agency=Inside the Hall |date=August 3, 2022}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://iuhoosiers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jalen-hood-schifino/16673 Indiana Hoosiers bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Hood-Schifino, Jalen}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Pittsburgh]] [[Category:Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Point guards]]
